title: Economics-Aware Feature Gating and Pricing Playbook
author: Marisol Alvarez
body:
Summary
This playbook defines a repeatable, cross-functional approach for gating features based on economic signals, aligning pricing and packaging to feature fidelity, and operating rollouts that can be reversed with minimal customer impact. The goal is to let product teams make data-driven gating decisions that preserve SLOs while protecting unit economics.

Background 
As Redwood adds more fidelity tiers, model variants, and adaptive behaviors (quantized fallbacks, streaming vs. batch modes), product teams must be able to:
- Gate features per-tenant or per-route when cost or capacity risk is elevated.
- Tie gates to pricing primitives (credits, bundles, fractional reserved capacity).
- Measure and revert without manual billing reconciliation or wrangling customer expectations.

Scope
This document covers:
- Product-level PRD for economics-aware feature gating.
- High-level design patterns for implementing gating in the runtime and control plane.
- Pricing/packaging guidance and standard billing primitives.
- Roadmap milestones and release criteria.
- Rollout and operational playbook including metrics, alerts, and rollback steps.

Definitions
- Fidelity: A class of output quality (e.g., high, medium, low) exposed as variant/sku.
- Gate: A conditional switch controlling whether a request path uses a feature (e.g., model variant, streaming) for a tenant/route.
- Credit Bucket: Time-bound credits applied to usage that can fund higher-fidelity consumption.
- Fractional Capacity: Reserved throughput expressed as an SLA-backed fraction of a GPU pool.

PRD (Product Requirements)
1) Requirements (must-have)
- Per-tenant gates: ability to enable/disable features at tenant, route, and token-budget granularity.
- Economics signals: gates can be triggered by on-chain signals in our metering (credits remaining < threshold), cost-per-token exceeding threshold, or latency SLO breaches.
- Billing integration: gated transitions must be visible in billing exports and the console within 5 minutes.
- Graceful fallback: when a gate disables a higher-fidelity path, the platform must automatically pick a compatible lower-fidelity variant (model fallback) and mark the output with metadata for QA and auditing.

2) Success metrics
- Reduction in emergency capacity spend from runaway fidelity by >75% in first 90 days after rollout.
- 95% of gated transitions reflected in billing CSV within 5 minutes.
- No customer-facing error rate increase >0.5% following gated fallbacks.

Design Spec (high-level)
1) Architecture glue points
- Control plane: Feature-gate service (FGS) stores gate policies (tenant->rules). Exposes HTTP API for evaluation and a streaming change feed for runtime.
- Runtime: Evaluate gate at request arrival. If gate denies high-fidelity path, mutate request routing to the chosen fallback variant and attach tag header X-Redwood-Gate:{gate_id}=denied.
- Billing: Billing pipeline subscribes to gate-change stream and annotated usage events to add bookkeeping fields (gated_by, fallback_variant, credit_charge).

2) Policy model (example)
- Rule: {"scope":"tenant","trigger":"credits_remaining <= 10%","action":"downgrade-to:medium-fidelity","cooldown":"30m"}
- Implementation note: Policy DSL is intentionally small to limit operator error. Support triggers: credits_remaining, cost_per_1k_tokens_7d, p95_latency_5m, manual.

3) Metadata and audit fields
The runtime will add the following tags to request logs and meter events (console displays these fields):
- gated_by (string), fallback_variant (string), gate_trigger (string), gate_version (semver).

4) Safety and consistency 
- Atomicity: Gate evaluation and chosen fallback must be performed before any tokens are emitted.
- Fallback compatibility: Only fallback variants that are API-compatible and included in the tenant's allowed variant list may be chosen.

Pricing and Packaging Guidance
1) Pricing primitives
- Fidelity credits: sellable bundles (e.g., High-Fidelity Credits: 100k token-equivalents). Credits consumed when requests use high-fidelity variants.
- Burst buffer: short-lived credit grants for spikes (auto-grant capped at 20% of monthly credits).
- Fractional reserved capacity: sell monthly commit for throughput and allow gating to reduce fidelity once committed capacity is reached.

2) Suggested SKUs and mapping
- freemium-tier: low fidelity only, throttled concurrency 
- standard-tier: medium fidelity + 25k HF credits included 
- pro-tier: medium+high fidelity, 200k HF credits included, fractional reserve 0.05 throughput unit

3) Billing behavior on gate-triggered fallbacks
- If the gate downgrades to medium fidelity: meter at the medium rate (no HF credit consumed).
- If the tenant has an outstanding chargeback exception: gates can be configured to apply dry-run (log only) until billing review complete.

Roadmap and Release Themes
- Q3 2026: Internal alpha of FGS + runtime evaluation for a single medium/high fidelity pair.
- Q4 2026: Billing integration and console visualization (per-tenant gating timeline).
- Q1 2027: Multi-rule policies, cooldowns, and manual override via Console.
- Q2 2027: Marketplace SKUs for fractional capacity + fidelity bundles.

Release Criteria (for GA)
- Feature-gate end-to-end path validated with 10 enterprise test tenants under production-like traffic.
- Billing exports show nested gated events and reconcile with ledger for sample month.
- UX: Console shows per-tenant gate status and historical timeline with drilldowns.

Operational Playbook (Runbook)
1) Pre-rollout checklist
- Add canary tenants in staging with representative traffic shapes.
- Configure billing pipeline to accept gated annotations.
- Verify audit logs include gated_by and gate_trigger.

2) Typical incident: unexpected mass gating
- Alert triggers: >5% of tenants experience automatic gate transitions within 5m.
- Pager duty: oncall-product + infra-sre.
- Steps:
  1. Identify rule causing mass gating via FGS change feed.
  2. If rule was automated (e.g., credits threshold miscalibrated), disable the rule (FGS API: POST /rules/{id}/disable).
  3. If billing miscount suspected, revert to dry-run mode (FGS: POST /rules/{id}/toggle-dryrun).
  4. Notify affected customers via support-sla@redwood and create a support ticket to reconcile billing.
  5. Postmortem owner: eng-platform.

3) Rollback procedure
- Criteria to rollback: billing mismatch >0.5% or customer complaint >3 in 24h.
- Steps:
  1. Put FGS into global manual mode (only manual approvals allowed).
  2. Issue immediate console update and customer comms.
  3. Reconcile ledger for impacted window and, if necessary, issue credits automatically via billing automation.

Metrics, Dashboards and Alerts
- GateRate: % of requests that are gated (per-tenant and global) — alert if >5% unexpected change in 5m.
- BillingLag: time from gated event to billing export — SLO 5m, alert if >10m for >1% of events.
- FallbackErrorRate: increase in 5xx following fallback — alert if delta >0.5%.
- EconomicLeak: estimated unexpected spend due to failed gating — run daily job to estimate and surface in finance dashboard.

Appendix A — Example policy JSON (DSL is simplified)
```
{
  "id": "gate-tenant-low-credits-01",
  "scope": "tenant:acme-corp",
  "trigger": "credits_remaining_percent <= 10",
  "action": "downgrade-to:medium-fidelity",
  "cooldown_minutes": 30,
  "dry_run": false
}
```

Appendix B — Console UX wireframes (text)
- Gate Timeline: left rail filter (tenant, rule, time window) + center timeline with colored bands (green=enabled, orange=dry-run, red=denied).
- Drilldown: shows sample request with headers and gated metadata; link to billing CSV entry.
